questions.name: Understand the key concepts of service management
questions.objective: 1.1 Recall the definition of service management, service, utility, warranty, customer, user, and sponsor
questions.text: Which statement best describes a service in ITIL 4?

answers.text: A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating outcomes that customers want to achieve without customers managing specific costs and risks
A physical device that is always owned by the service consumer
A contract that guarantees every risk is removed from the customer
A department that performs technology support activities for internal users

explanations.a: A service helps customers achieve desired outcomes while the provider manages specified costs and risks. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Missing-word logic 1: regarding Service, service is not limited to physical ownership; ITIL 4 describes how value is enabled through outcomes.
explanations.c: Exam wording 1: regarding Service, service can reduce or manage specified risks, but ITIL 4 does not define it as eliminating every risk.
explanations.d: Consumer-side clue 1: regarding Service, service is broader than a department; it is the means of enabling value co-creation.

questions.name: Understand the key concepts of service management
questions.objective: 1.1 Recall the definition of service management, service, utility, warranty, customer, user, and sponsor
questions.text: Identify the missing word(s): [?] is a set of specialized organizational capabilities for enabling value for customers in the form of services.

answers.text: Service consumption
Service management
Warranty
Service offering

explanations.a: Learning outcome clue 2: regarding Service management, service management is the provider capability, while service consumption covers consumer activities when using services.
explanations.b: Service management is the specialized capability used to enable customer value through services. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Relationship clue 2: regarding Service management, service management is the overall capability, while warranty is assurance that a service is fit for use.
explanations.d: Recall check 2: regarding Service management, service management is the capability set, while a service offering describes one or more services made available to consumers.

questions.name: Understand the key concepts of service management
questions.objective: 1.1 Recall the definition of service management, service, utility, warranty, customer, user, and sponsor
questions.text: Which phrase describes utility in ITIL 4?

answers.text: The activity of managing supplier contracts
The assurance that a service will meet agreed requirements
The functionality offered by a product or service to meet a particular need
The perceived benefits, usefulness, and importance of something

explanations.a: Usage clue 3: regarding Utility, utility concerns service functionality, not supplier management activities.
explanations.b: Syllabus match 3: regarding Utility, utility concerns functionality and purpose; the assurance aspect is warranty.
explanations.c: Utility describes what the service does and whether it is fit for purpose. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Scenario clue 3: regarding Utility, utility supports value, but the perceived benefit itself is value.

questions.name: Understand the key concepts of service management

questions.text: Identify the missing word(s): In ITIL 4, the term related to this statement is [?]. Which phrase describes warranty in ITIL 4?

answers.text: The functionality that enables the customer outcome

questions.name: Understand the key concepts of service management
questions.objective: 1.1 Recall the definition of service management, service, utility, warranty, customer, user, and sponsor
questions.text: In ITIL 4, who is the customer?

answers.text: A person who defines requirements for services and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption
A person who authorizes the budget for service consumption
A person who manages the provider's internal processes
A person who uses services every day
